auditor: muse-spark-1.3 (Meta Model API), one call per section, reasoning_effort low
scope: compiled facts vs the handbook pages they cite (card backs are byte copies of these facts); exam items and lesson narration not checked in this pass

flagged.issue: Omits that a designee may also sign the school note.
flagged.suggested_fix: Four exceptions need four different signers: physician for medical need, principal, dean, or designee for school, employer for work, and parent or legal guardian for family.

flagged.issue: The page describes eLearning as a renewal option but does not state it can never substitute for the original-license knowledge test.
flagged.suggested_fix: eLearning may be an alternative testing option when renewing your driver's license.

flagged.issue: The page states the address-change does not provide a new card, but does not state the record-versus-reissue distinction.
flagged.suggested_fix: An address change does not automatically provide a new license; a replacement may be requested for a fee.

flagged.issue: Cited page 22 does not state buses as qualifying HOV users.
flagged.suggested_fix: HOV lanes take qualifying carpools per posted counts and hours, decal low-emission cars and motorcycles, with diamonds and Carpool Lane paint, open only at marked entries.

flagged.issue: Statement omits stop and leave prohibitions for bus lanes.
flagged.suggested_fix: Bus lanes ban driving, stopping, parking or leaving a vehicle but let you cross to turn.

flagged.issue: Statement omits passengers for yellow and standing/parking for red.
flagged.suggested_fix: Yellow loads and unloads passengers and freight on posted time with driver staying with noncommercial vehicle, red bans stopping, standing or parking except marked buses.

flagged.issue: Cited page 22 does not state buses as qualifying HOV users.
flagged.suggested_fix: HOV lanes admit posted carpools, decal low-emission vehicles and motorcycles through marked entries, unlike the center lane usable 200 feet to turn.

flagged.issue: Statement omits unless NO TURN ON RED bars it exception.
flagged.suggested_fix: Red lights permit the turn after a full stop unless NO TURN ON RED bars it, red arrows forbid it, bus lanes may only be crossed.

flagged.issue: Statement omits passengers for yellow and standing/parking for red.
flagged.suggested_fix: White for passenger loading, green for posted short stays, yellow for passengers and freight with driver staying, red bans stopping, standing or parking except marked buses, blue for placards.

flagged.issue: Page lists six exceptions including approaching a right turn and one-way roads, which the statement omits.
flagged.suggested_fix: Slow riders hug the right curb except when passing, turning left, avoiding hazards, narrow lanes, approaching a right turn, or on a one-way with two-plus lanes.

flagged.issue: Page 40 does not state the flashing-red stop rule used for the comparison.
flagged.suggested_fix: Flashing yellow needs no stop, flashing yellow arrows leave the turn unprotected unlike green arrows, green demands yielding and exit room, and dark signals default to all-way stops.

flagged.issue: Page does not state the contrast about normal intersections following arrows and signs.
flagged.suggested_fix: Roundabouts use yield-on-entry and counterclockwise circulation, with right-lane rights for right turns and entry-lane exits for straights.

flagged.issue: Page 53 lists only two right-edge exceptions; the full list continues on the next page.
flagged.suggested_fix: Cyclist duties add helmet, visibility, and right-edge rules, night gear is lamp, rear light, and reflectors with distance ratings, and page 53 lists passing and left-turn exceptions with more exceptions on the next page.

flagged.issue: Page 67 does not state the four-wheel ABS firm-pressure rule, which appears on the prior page.
flagged.suggested_fix: To get out of a locked-wheel skid on page 67: for rear ABS ease and steer into skid, for front ABS release and straighten, without ABS pump, and dry wet brakes with gas plus brake.

flagged.issue: Page 75 does not state free tow to a CHP-approved location, the will-not list, or 511 for FSP, which are on the next page.
flagged.suggested_fix: During commute times FSP will provide a gallon of gas, jump start, refill radiator and tape hoses, change a flat, and report a collision to CHP.

flagged.issue: Page 67 does not state the four-wheel ABS firm-pressure rule or the wet/snow/ice staircase fully on that page alone.
flagged.suggested_fix: On page 67, rear ABS eases then steers into skid, front ABS releases and straightens, non-ABS pumps with downshift and emergency brake, and wet roads reduce 5-10 mph, packed snow by half, ice to 5 mph.

flagged.issue: Page 75 does not state free tow to a CHP-approved location or the will-not exclusions, which are on the next page.
flagged.suggested_fix: On page 75, watch gauges with heat and cold care, pull to the right shoulder with right-side return and belted waiting, and FSP provides gas, jumps, radiator refills, flat changes, and collision reports.

flagged.issue: The page limits the licensing delay to up to one year, not a fixed year-long delay.
flagged.suggested_fix: Under-21 drivers caught with alcohol face impound up to 30 days plus possible fine and one-year suspension, or a licensing delay of up to one year if unlicensed.

flagged.issue: The page says actions may occur, not that they will occur as stated.
flagged.suggested_fix: Officers suspecting under-21 drinking may require tests; at 0.01% DMV may revoke for a year plus a licensed DUI program, at 0.05% PAS officers may require further tests, and confirmed 0.05% may lead to arrest and suspension.

flagged.issue: The page allows you or your representative to file and gives a website without stating online-only, which the fact omits.
flagged.suggested_fix: Each driver, or their representative, must file SR 1 at dmv.ca.gov/accidentreport whether or not at fault and even on private property.

flagged.issue: The page requires more than $1,000 and allows filing by a representative, which the summary imprecisely condenses.
flagged.suggested_fix: DMV reporting is required within 10 days if damage is more than $1,000 or any injury/death occurs, with each driver or representative filing SR 1 regardless of fault or private property.
